drop_off_rule: Show items published within the last 7 days. Remove any item more than 14 days after its date_published, even if fewer than 10 items remain.

items.title: Microsoft: treat deployed AI agents as insider threats
items.summary: Microsoft's official blog argues that frontier models, whatever their origin, can't be trusted, and that enterprises need guardian agents that watch and moderate every action of their own agents before it happens, extending its Project Perception security system to internal agents.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Enterprise security teams will now expect agent deployments to come with per-action monitoring, least-privilege tool access and audit trails, so build those into the design rather than bolting them on.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt open models for agents
items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120B multimodal model for always-on enterprise agents, plus Bolt 74B-A9B for local workstations now and Bolt E4B (4GB) on Oct 23.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Gives you an open agent model at server, workstation and edge sizes that customers can post-train on their data and run on their own NVIDIA hardware.

items.title: GitHub Copilot retired GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.7 Flash and Grok 4.5 on Oct 19
items.summary: GitHub deprecated six models across Copilot Chat, agent mode and completions on Oct 19, 2026, pointing users to GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash and Grok 4.7 instead.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Customer workflows pinned to these models break now; Copilot Enterprise admins may need to enable the replacement models in their model policies.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon is now generally available
items.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Argon, its new frontier model, to developers, enterprises and consumers. Introductory API price is $2/M input and $10/M output tokens, with cached input 95% off. Google says it ranks #1 on the Vals Index.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: A new frontier option at aggressive pricing, aimed at multi-step finance, legal and coding work. Expect customers to ask for bake-offs against their current model.

items.title: GitHub ships a REST API for Copilot model policies
items.summary: GET and PATCH endpoints for Copilot model policies are now generally available at the enterprise, enterprise team, enterprise app and organization levels.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Lets you script which models each customer org or team can use, instead of clicking through settings, which helps with rollouts and model deprecations.

items.title: Hugging Face libraries add native support for TorchNeuron on AWS Trainium
items.summary: TorchNeuron, a native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium with eager mode, torch.compile, FSDP and TP, enters public beta Oct 20, and Transformers, Diffusers and Kernels support it directly.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Makes Trainium a more realistic lower-cost option for AWS customers who want to train or serve open models without rewriting code for a compiler-first stack.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an open-weight frontier multimodal MoE
items.summary: Meta published Muse Spark Open on Hugging Face. It is an open-weight mixture-of-experts model that takes text, image, video and audio, with a 1M-token context window.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Gives FDEs a self-hostable multimodal frontier model for customers with data-residency or on-prem limits.

items.title: Reflection AI releases Beam, a 501B open model
items.summary: Reflection AI released Beam, a 501B-parameter open model that runs at about the speed of a 23B model. It ships BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints, with vLLM and SGLang deployment recipes.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: A large open model that customers can own and fine-tune. The ready vLLM and SGLang recipes cut the time to a private deployment.

items.title: Cursor cloud agents get canvases, an Environments API and 300-repo environments
items.summary: Cursor cloud agents can now build and share interactive canvases. An Environments API is in beta for creating agent environments programmatically, and environments now support up to 300 repos and load large ones 5x faster.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: The Environments API lets FDEs script reproducible multi-repo agent setups for each customer instead of hand-building them.

items.title: GitHub agentic autofix for code scanning alerts is GA
items.summary: Code scanning alerts can be assigned to Copilot, which explores the codebase, proposes a fix, re-runs CodeQL to check it, and opens a draft PR. It is available to Code Security and Advanced Security customers on Enterprise Cloud.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: A production pattern for a verified agent loop (fix, validate, PR) that enterprise security teams can adopt now.

items.title: GitHub Copilot deprecates several models on Nov 16, 2026
items.summary: On Nov 16, GitHub will retire Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra across all Copilot experiences. Suggested replacements are Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Luna.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Customer workflows pinned to these models will break mid-November. Audit model policies and integrations now.

items.title: Vercel Drives: persistent storage for agents is GA
items.summary: Vercel Drives keeps an agent's files independent of its execution environment. Agents can mount the same drive in a new Vercel Sandbox and continue where they left off.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Solves the state-across-runs problem for long-running agents without custom storage plumbing.

items.title: Vercel AI Gateway index: open-weight models take 71.5% of tokens, 23% of spend
items.summary: Vercel's October production index (September data) shows open-weight models processing more than 7 in 10 gateway tokens. AI spend is up 13x while cost per token has halved, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash alone handled nearly half of all tokens.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Real production data for cost conversations: route high-volume work to open weights and keep frontier models for the hard steps.

items.title: Third Moment Research runs 10,000 concurrent agents for 36+ hours on OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI case study: Third Moment runs 10,000 agents at once on 36-48 hour sessions. It uses Codex as a subagent inside an outer GPT-6 Sol harness, cut a backtest from about 3 hours to about 3-5 minutes, and uses Daybreak to pen-test its sandboxes.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: A concrete reference architecture for very long-horizon agents: an outer supervisor harness, fixing token-wasting polling, and automated sandbox security testing.

items.title: MCP Events support in Vercel Connect is in public beta
items.summary: Vercel Connect, the eve framework and AI SDK now support the MCP Events extension. Agents subscribe to webhook events from MCP servers, and Vercel renews subscriptions and verifies signatures automatically.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Moves customer agents from polling to event-driven triggers on new issues, messages or document feedback.
